# Browser and headless Chromium

## What this machine has

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Interactive browsing, clicks, forms, live page screenshots | `browse` MCP server (drives Brave through the browse extension) |
| Headless DOM dump, screenshot, PDF, CDP | `google-chrome` |
| Fallback when the Playwright cache is empty | `brave --headless=new` |

`google-chrome`, `google-chrome-stable`, `chrome`, `chromium` and
`chrome-headless-shell` are wrappers in `~/.local/bin`. The wrapper picks the
newest Chrome for Testing in `~/.cache/ms-playwright`. If that cache is empty,
the wrapper runs Brave.

Chrome for Testing is version 149. Brave is version 1.100.58.

## Commands

1. DOM dump: `timeout 60 google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --dump-dom https://example.com`.
2. Screenshot: `timeout 60 google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --screenshot=/tmp/page.png --window-size=1280,900 https://example.com`.
3. PDF: `timeout 60 google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --print-to-pdf=/tmp/page.pdf https://example.com`.
4. Remote debugging: `google-chrome --headless=new --remote-debugging-port=9222 https://example.com`.

## Rules

1. Do not add `--no-sandbox` on this machine. The sandbox works.
2. Use `--headless=new`. Do not use the old `--headless`.
3. Add `--disable-gpu` for server-side rendering. Remove it only when WebGL must work.
4. Put `timeout 60` in front of every headless call. A page that waits forever blocks the agent.
5. Puppeteer, Playwright and Lighthouse read `CHROME_PATH` and `CHROME_BIN`. Keep them at `~/.local/bin/google-chrome`.

## Repair

1. Check the wrapper: `google-chrome --version` prints `Google Chrome for Testing 149.0.7827.55`.
2. Check the cache: `ls ~/.cache/ms-playwright`.
3. Refill the cache: `npx playwright install chromium`.
4. Check the fallback: `brave --version`.
